title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2611.14241v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We introduce DyShip, a framework for classifying speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations in the Seamless Interaction corpus. We compare five speech representations: spectrograms, MFCCs, self-supervised WavLM representations, x-vectors, and estimated articulatory movements. Spectral features perform best for familiarity classification, reaching an accuracy of 87.81%, while WavLM achieves the highest kinship accuracy of 85.17%. X-vectors and articulatory features yield weaker results on familiarity classifiaction, but shine for kinship classification, with an AUC of 0.909 for x-vectors. Most classifiers exceed previously reported human and audio language model scores on the same dataset. These findings highlight the potential of conventional acoustic features for relationship inference and motivate further investigation of the conversational cues captured by different representations.

translated_title: Dyship：利用声学特征从双人对话中进行说话人关系分类
translated_abstract: 我们提出了DyShip，这是一个用于从Seamless Interaction语料库的双人对话中对说话人熟悉度和亲缘关系进行分类的框架。我们比较了五种语音表示方式：频谱图、梅尔频率倒谱系数（MFCCs）、自监督WavLM表示、x向量以及估计的发音运动。频谱特征在熟悉度分类上表现最佳，准确率达到87.81%，而WavLM在亲缘关系分类上取得了最高的85.17%准确率。x向量和发音特征在熟悉度分类上结果较弱，但在亲缘关系分类上表现出色，其中x向量的AUC达到0.909。大多数分类器在同一数据集上的表现超过了此前报告的人类和音频语言模型的分数。这些发现凸显了传统声学特征在关系推断方面的潜力，并激励人们进一步研究不同表示方式所捕获的对话线索。
tldr: 该论文提出DyShip框架，通过比较频谱图、MFCC、WavLM、x向量和发音运动五种声学表示，从双人对话中实现说话人熟悉度和亲缘关系的自动分类，且多数分类器表现超越人类和音频语言模型基准。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DyShip, a framework that leverages five acoustic representations (spectrograms, MFCCs, WavLM, x-vectors, and articulatory features) to classify speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations, with most classifiers surpassing previously reported human and audio language model scores.
